raw_recipe.headline: D's Famous Salsa
raw_recipe.description: This salsa with canned tomatoes is easy to make in a food processor with onion, garlic, lime juice, chiles, and cilantro for a smooth or chunky dip.

video.description: A fast and delicious salsa from easy ingredients you may already have on hand.

review.reviewBody: Thie recipe was amazing. The only things I would suggest are 1. buying Hunt's tomatoes - don't substitute with a generic brand. 2. draining the tomatoes, unless you like a really runny salsa. 3. only blending on pulse a few times - I'm talking seconds. The first batch I made was very runny, but the second one was AMAZING, and I got so many compliments on it!! :) Thanks!

Wonderful tasting salsa. I did do a few changes in the recipe. I used Mexican stewed tomatoes, fresh jalapeno's, lemon juice in place of lime, lots of cilantro and added about a teaspoon of chili powder to mine. All our favorite Mexican restaurants tell us to use the chili powder. Thanks for the recipe.

I loved this but I don't like uncooked canned tomatoes so I used fresh Roma, my garden is full in summer so I make this as often as I can. Always a hit at get together's. Try the fresh tomatoes you won't be sorry.

Words cannot describe how I feel about this recipe. It's soooo good. I was skeptical that it could really taste fresh with canned tomatoes, but it truly does. I didn't change a thing and it was mild and flavorful. When you originally chop your onions, leave them a little on the big side, that way when you blend them, they won't be puried and be overpowering. Also, don't over blend the salsa. After reading reviews, it seems some have complained about the consistency, that it's too runny. I didn't drain my tomatoes, but only pulsed my blender a few times. The consistency was perfect. I've eaten chips and salsa for lunch 2 days in a row now. I'm addicted and will make this regularly. Thanks so much!

I made it the day before I needed it for "Easy Mexican dish" here. I took heed of the tip from another member to drain the tomatoes first. I pulsed everything "except the diced tomatoes" first & then tossed in the tomatoes. I was not sure what "canned sliced green chiles" is referring to, so I used canned sliced jalapenos. I also used a white onion for a sweeter flavor. Turned out really good. Next time I will use Hunt's diced tomatoes like another member suggested.

I used 5 very ripe tomatoes from my garden. I chopped them first and put in a strainer to drain then halved the recipe. I put all the rest of ingredients in my small bowl of the food processor and pulsed them and put them in a bowl. Next I added the chopped, drained tomatoes. I didn't put the tomatoes in the food processor because I prefer them in larger chunks-yummy! In the winter I plan to make this recipe with stewed tomatoes. But then again I would drain the tomatoes first. Thanks Denise

It was really good! As ever, I made some changes - some of necessity, some of choice. Used 1 14-oz can of (drained) diced tomatoes, 2 whole scallions, about double that amount of lime, a homegrown fresh chile, about double that amount of cilantro, and also added hot spanish paprika and maybe 1/2 tsp each of powdered garlic & onion. I would definitely make this again.

I used only one can of stewed tomatoes and substituted the chili for a single habanero and simply added everything whole into the processor and it turned out amazing and made everything quick and easy

This recipe leaves a runny and bland salsa, I am pretty concerned about those who tried it without some extra steps. But you can make this recipe good, by draining your canned tomatoes with a colander and adding some cumin and a pinch of garam masala

Delicious! Have made three times already this week. Good as written or with plain old Hunts diced tomatoes. To make it easy: a half batch is one can tomatoes, 1/4 cup finely diced onion, 1 large clove garlic finely diced, 1 1/2 tsp dried cilantro when fresh isn't handy, 1/2 TB lime juice. Our preference is to drain tomatoes (just drink the juice!) and use hand mixer only on tomatoes. Everything else is finely chopped and mixed in. Boiling the jalapeños for ten minutes, cooling and dicing works great! Thanks for a keeper!

I've made this recipe with some modifications and I love it! Very simple to make especially if you use a food processor. 

I substituted a few of the ingredients:

Green Chilies - Replaced with sliced jalapeño peppers
1/2 lime - 1 tbsp of lemon juice OR 1/2 lime juiced (turned out great both ways)
Stewed Tomatoes - Used canned diced tomatoes.

I used the canned tomatoes because I have quite a few cans that are supposedly past the "best by" date and it has worked out great. When I run out of those I will try it with the stew tomatoes and see how I like it. But fantastic recipe!

I don't know how many times I've made this recipe, even with tweaks here and there it comes out perfect. I use Rotel instead of diced tomatoes and usually more cilantro and garlic and fresh jalapenos from the garden. It is fantastic!
This is an excellent basic salsa recipe, easy to customize. I turned up the heat with black pepper and taco seasoning. Tasted really good.
not the best not the worst did not taste great
It's perfect! Wouldn't change a thing!
This is gorgeous salsa! Thank you. I used chilis from the garden because they were ripe and everyone raved about the salsa

The first batch, I made the recipe as written with the exception of fire roasted tomatoes. The second batch, I used fire roasted tomatoes, jalapeno, chili powder, and cumin along with the other ingredients listed. Easy to make, doesn't take much time, and delicious!
Been making this recipe forever!yummy!!!!
I seen on here to try with hunts stewed tomatoes and its absolutely delicious .... Not to spicy but not to mild
YUMMY 😋
